setup: Position an incline bench set to approximately 30 to 45 degrees inside the Smith machine.
Align the bench so the bar lowers directly across your upper chest, just below the collarbones.
Lie back on the bench, retract and depress your shoulder blades, and plant your feet firmly on the floor.
Grasp the bar with a pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, rotating the hooks to unrack the bar.
steps: Lower the bar under control toward your upper chest, maintaining tucked elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle to your torso.
Touch lightly or pause just above the clavicular area without letting the bar bounce or rest on your chest.
Press the bar upward explosively along the fixed track until your arms are extended but not harshly locked out.
Rotate the wrists to re-rack the bar securely onto the safety catches at the end of the set.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower the bar to your chest, and exhale forcefully as you press past the sticking point.
cues: Keep your upper back pinned to the bench
Tuck elbows slightly rather than flaring

common_faults.fault: Bench aligned too far forward or backward relative to the bar track.
common_faults.correction: Adjust the bench position before loading weight so the bar tracks comfortably to the upper sternum without straining the shoulders.

common_faults.fault: Excessive elbow flaring at ninety degrees.
common_faults.correction: Keep elbows tucked to approximately 45–60 degrees relative to your sides to protect the rotator cuff.

common_faults.fault: Excessive arching of the lower back.
common_faults.correction: Maintain firm foot pressure and a natural lumbar arch while keeping your glutes and upper back glued to the bench pad.

precautions: Set the mechanical safety stops on the Smith machine to chest level before beginning your sets.
